headline: High: Plandex can write and execute against shared project files while Dexter has broad network egress and financial-data access, creating leakage and cascading-action risk if paired without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can emit autonomous outputs into .dexter/scratchpad/ and Plandex reads/writes a project directory with review-then-apply. If Dexter content is copied into Plandex plans, prompt-like text can steer actions. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is plausible though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Dexter outputs are pasted or synced into Plandex plan files
IF Plandex treats project-file content as instructions rather than untrusted text
mitigations: Keep Dexter and Plandex in separate directories
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Manually strip instruction-like text before import
Use a provenance header for all copied snippets
requires-engineering: add content-tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs. Plandex also has broad network egress and reads/writes the project directory. If shared files contain sensitive financial material, either agent can move it into external services, making leakage plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF shared project files contain financial or market data
IF either agent forwards file contents to an external API or model provider
mitigations: Store sensitive data outside the shared workspace
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs
Use redacted fixtures instead of live financial data
Review outbound requests before execution
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, while Plandex supports multiple instances with shared state via a backend and can modify git state and the filesystem. Overlapping write paths create coordination risk on shared workspaces, though Plandex’s sandbox reduces direct damage.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or directory
IF concurrent runs modify the same files or branch
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Run only one writer at a time
Use file-level locks for shared paths
Stage changes before merge
requires-engineering: add orchestrator locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter can autonomously produce research outputs from external APIs, and Plandex is a planner that can apply changes after review. If Plandex treats Dexter’s outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into committed code or plans. The pair lacks a built-in verification link, so the unsafe path is default-plausible.
conditions: IF Plandex imports Dexter-generated facts or citations without independent verification
IF those outputs are used to create or apply code changes
mitigations: Require a human review step between agents
Cross-check Dexter outputs against source data
Mark Dexter outputs as untrusted in Plandex
Disable auto-apply for Dexter-derived plans
requires-engineering: add verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter touches financial data and market data, while Plandex handles source code and may send content to a cloud or self-hosted server and model provider. If financial data is embedded in code or plans, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is placed into Plandex-managed files or prompts
IF the chosen Plandex backend retains or logs that content beyond policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plandex prompts
Use synthetic or masked datasets
Confirm retention settings before use
Separate compliance-sensitive workflows
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
